api.no_server: The server does not answer: is the app still running?
app.bar.dcs_config: DCS controls: devices, hat views, backups
app.columns.tip: Drag to widen or narrow; double-click: default width
app.export.all_hint: {n} modules: the aircraft with a device ticked
app.export.all_none: No aircraft with a device ticked
app.kneeboard.all_folder: Saved Games\DCS\Kneeboard\, one folder per aircraft
app.kneeboard.not_aircraft: This profile is not an aircraft: no kneeboard
app.kneeboard.writes_to: Writes the pages to Saved Games\DCS\Kneeboard\{unit}\
app.pdf.tip: PDF of the module, one page per ticked device (Ctrl+P); the arrow: every module
bindings.intro: tick what you want to remove from DCS. DCS must be closed; the whole controls folder is backed up first.
bindings.not_installed: This module is not installed: without its defaults, its bindings cannot be computed again.
bindings.origin.device_tip: The module has it for this very device.
bindings.origin.generic_tip: The module has nothing for this device: DCS gives it what it gives any joystick (gun trigger on button 1…). Often worth removing.
bindings.origin.user_tip: You set it in the DCS controls screen.
bindings.partial_detail: The others were no longer in the DCS files.
bindings.title: Bindings: {device}
bindings.unknown_tip: This DCS command's number is unknown to the app: it could not write its removal the way the game does. Remove it in the DCS controls screen.
dcs.absent.intro: These devices have saved controls, but DCS did not see them at its last two starts
dcs.absent.intro2: Unplugged that day, or gone for good: your call. "Forget" deletes their controls in every module, after a backup.
dcs.absent.no_log: DCS's log names no device: no way to tell which are absent. Start DCS once, with the devices plugged in.
dcs.absent.none: None: DCS saw every device that has controls.
dcs.absent.title: Absent devices
dcs.backup.title: Backups
dcs.devices.intro: A disabled device is ignored by DCS, in every module; its controls are kept and come back when it is enabled again. It is the "Disable" setting of the game's controls screen.
dcs.devices.title: Devices disabled in DCS
dcs.forget.label: Forget
dcs.generic.all_modules: Every installed module, not only those where the device is configured (creates a file per module)
dcs.generic.confirm: A single backup is made before; the controls are read again after writing.
dcs.generic.intro: When a module has nothing for a device, DCS gives it the buttons of "any joystick": rudder pedals get a weapon release on button 2, nosewheel steering on 4… Tick the devices that have neither button nor hat; their generic buttons are removed in every module. What you put there yourself, what the module has for this device, and the axes stay.
dcs.generic.none_configured: No generic button on these devices in the modules where they are configured.
dcs.generic.none_installed: No generic button on these devices in the installed modules.
dcs.generic.title: Devices without buttons
dcs.generic.unknown: Not removable, DCS command number unknown to the app: {list}; to remove in the game's controls screen.
dcs.hat.all_modules: Every installed module, not only those you configured (creates a file per module)
dcs.hat.confirm: A single backup is made before, restorable below; the controls are read again after writing.
dcs.hat.every_device: Every device, hats in use included
dcs.hat.intro: Every module puts the 8 slow views ("View Up slow"…) on the first hat of every device, even rudder pedals, an ICP or an MFD. With TrackIR or VR they are useless and clutter the pages. Only these 8 default bindings are removed; what you put on a hat yourself stays.
dcs.hat.none_configured: No device carries these views in the configured modules.
dcs.hat.none_installed: No device carries these views in the installed modules.
dcs.hat.not_written: {file} ({profile}): in the preview, nothing was written
dcs.hat.title: Hat views
dcs.hat.used_hint: : tick "Every device" to remove its default views all the same
dcs.intro: Before each change to the DCS controls, the app backs up the whole {folder} folder. The last 20 backups are kept.
dcs.modifiers.deleted: These modules have no modifiers file any more: DCS deletes it when only the default settings are left in it, which happens when it ignores a modifier. A backup still has it; it comes back with the device names repaired. If you deleted it yourself, leave it.
dcs.modifiers.intro: These modifiers name their device by an old name: its driver renamed it, the GUID is the same. DCS ignores them, and the bindings that use them show but do not work in the game. "Repair" gives them the name DCS uses now, in every module, after a backup.
dcs.modifiers.title: Modifiers
dcs.restore.confirm: The DCS controls will go back exactly to this state, for every module; the current state is backed up first.
dcs.restore.detail: The state before is itself backed up, at the top of the list.
dcs.restore.label: Restore
dcs.result.deleted: File deleted, as DCS does when no difference with the default settings is left: {files}. This device no longer shows in these modules of the app: nothing is lost.
dcs.result.differ: Read again after writing, differences with the preview:
dcs.result.ok: Read again after writing: as previewed.
dcs.running: DCS is running: close it to restore or change its controls, it writes these files again when saving.
dcs.running_unknown: Cannot tell whether DCS is running: changes will be refused.
dcs.see_window: : see the details in the window
dcs.title: DCS controls
dcs.undo.detail: The DCS controls are back to how they were before.
dcs.undo.label: Undo this removal
devices.disabled_tip: Disabled in DCS: the game ignores this device (DCS controls window)
devices.hide_tip: Hide this device in every module (H)
devices.hint: Ticked = pages exported · drag for the order of the pages
devices.none: No device configured for this module.
devices.title: Devices
editor.check.hint: Press every button of the device: its box lights up, or the editor offers to place it.
editor.check.label: Check (V)
editor.check.mark_tip: Every button was tried and lands in the right box
editor.check.title: Check the numbering
editor.check.unboxed: {input} has no box: click on the picture where this button is
editor.delete.label: Delete the template
editor.delete.own_version: Delete your version of "{name}"? The library's comes back.
editor.delete.template: Delete the template "{name}"? It leaves your library.
editor.device_placeholder: DCS name, without GUID, then Enter
editor.discard: The unsaved changes will be lost. Continue?
editor.drop: Drop here a photo or a drawing of the device (PNG, JPG, SVG), or click to choose one.
editor.drop_hint: Or start from an existing template, on the left, to correct it.
editor.extra_box_tip: The same input drawn somewhere else
editor.identify.appeared: {device} just appeared: press the button once more
editor.identify.label: Identify (I)
editor.identify.tip: Press the device's button: the input is recognised
editor.import.label: Import…
editor.keys.check: check: press every button of the device
editor.keys.place: place an input (then click on the picture)
editor.name: Template name
editor.no_gamepad_api: This browser gives no access to game controllers (Gamepad API).
editor.no_input: No input: drag "＋ Input" onto the picture, or N then click.
editor.overrides_tip: Once saved, your template comes before the library's
editor.picture_expected: PNG, JPG or SVG picture expected
editor.placing: Click on the picture where the button is: {input}. Esc to cancel.
editor.preview.choose: Choose a module and a device to see the template with its bindings.
editor.split.hint_off: For a drawing too wide for one page: a cut line, to place between two parts.
editor.split.hint_on: Drag the blue line through a white area, between two parts of the drawing (a throttle's base and its handles).
editor.split.title: Kneeboard pages
modules.title: Modules
page.no_template: no template for this device: list of the commands
page.off_template: OFF TEMPLATE — bound in DCS, no box on the drawing
preview.bindings_tip: Every binding of this device in this module, to remove some from DCS
preview.create_tip: Create a template for this device
preview.diff_only_tip: Only the changes saved in Saved Games are known: the module's defaults are missing.
preview.edit_tip: Edit the template in the editor
preview.layers.label: Layers
preview.path_too_long_tip: The path of its controls file is longer than 260 characters: DCS's interpreter cannot read it, the page shows the module's defaults. A shorter Saved Games folder solves it.
preview.programs_tip: Buttons used by SRS, VectorXR or a program entered by hand
preview.template.label: Template
preview.template.manual_tip: Chosen by hand, for this device in every module. The template its name matches is "{name}": click to go back to it.
preview.title: Page
preview.unchecked_tip: This template's numbering has not been checked on the real device yet: a command may land in the wrong box. Edit the template, then "Check": press each button.
programs.error.input: Choose the button in the list, or press it with "Identify".
programs.error.missing: Enter the program and what the button does.
programs.intro: The buttons other programs use show on the pages beside the DCS commands, each in its colour. SRS and VectorXR are read directly; the others are entered here.
programs.srs.label: SRS profile for {module}
programs.srs.missing: SRS not found: enter its folder in the settings, "Other programs" tab.
programs.srs.none: None: no SRS on these pages
programs.title: Other programs on this device
progress.stopping: Stopping at the end of this module…
settings.devices.intro: Tick the devices to show. A hidden device leaves the lists and the exports of every module: a vJoy, a device unplugged for good. Applied at once.
settings.install.empty: Empty: found in the Windows registry
settings.install.label: DCS install folder
settings.language.hint: The names as DCS shows them, translated by its {l10n} files
settings.language.label: Commands language
settings.page_height.hint: The width is that of DCS's kneeboard frame (two thirds of the height), the drawing centred in it.
settings.page_height.label: Height of the kneeboard pages (pixels)
settings.page_height.missing: Enter the height of the pages, between 256 and 4096 pixels.
settings.programs.intro: The buttons other programs use show on the pages, each in its colour. SRS and VectorXR are read directly, never changing their settings; the others are entered from a device's page, "Other programs" button.
settings.programs.none: No program: neither SRS nor VectorXR found, nothing entered by hand.
settings.saved_games.label: DCS Saved Games folder
settings.split_wide.hint: (the WinWing throttles; the editor places it). Applied at once.
settings.split_wide.label: Cut into two pages the drawings that have a cut line
settings.srs.empty: Empty: found in the Windows registry, else in Program Files
settings.srs.label: SRS folder
settings.title: Settings
settings.ui_language.hint: The language of the menus and messages, and of the documentation opened from the app. Applied at once.
settings.ui_language.label: Interface language
settings.vectorxr.read.one: {n} button read in {file} (modules turned off do not count).
settings.vectorxr.read.other: {n} buttons read in {file} (modules turned off do not count).
shortcuts.editor: The template editor has its own shortcuts, listed in its column
shortcuts.export: Include the device in the export or not
shortcuts.hide: Hide or show the device, in every module
shortcuts.kneeboard: Export the module to the kneeboard
shortcuts.kneeboard_all: Export every module to its kneeboard
shortcuts.layers: Layers: on the same page / one page per layer
shortcuts.move: Move the device (order of the pages)
shortcuts.pdf_all: PDF of every module, in a single file
shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.zoom: Zoom on the page (buttons beside it: whole page, full width)
store.inactive_modifier: {names}: DCS ignores this modifier, its device changed its name. Its bindings show but do not work in the game. Repair it in the DCS controls window.
